nodes.name: Lenga beech
nodes.desc: A deciduous southern beech that forms the dense high-latitude forests of the southern Andes. It tolerates hard frost and heavy snow and regrows easily after fire.

nodes.name: Ñire
nodes.desc: A hardy southern beech of the forest edge, where the Magellanic forest meets the dry Patagonian steppe.

nodes.name: Steppe tussock grasses
nodes.desc: Tough bunchgrasses of the dry steppe east of the mountains, the main grazing for guanacos and hares.

nodes.name: Calafate
nodes.desc: A spiny shrub of the steppe and forest edge that bears dark berries in summer.

nodes.name: Prickly heath
nodes.desc: A low evergreen shrub with berries that GloBI records as food for birds such as the austral thrush.

nodes.name: Upland goose
nodes.desc: A grazing goose of grassland and wet meadows, one of the best-recorded birds around the park.

nodes.name: Austral thrush
nodes.desc: A common thrush of forests and gardens that eats berries and invertebrates.

nodes.name: Olive grass mouse
nodes.desc: A small rodent of steppe and forest edge, eating seeds, plants and insects. It is staple prey for foxes and raptors.

nodes.name: European hare
nodes.desc: An introduced grazer. GloBI records it as prey of pumas, culpeos, caracaras and condors.

nodes.name: Guanaco
nodes.desc: A wild camelid that grazes grasses, shrubs, herbs and lichens on the steppe. Its natural predators include the puma and the culpeo.

nodes.name: Huemul
nodes.desc: An endangered Andean deer of scrub and forest borders. Lenga is a common item in its diet, and the puma is its only natural predator.

nodes.name: Wood-boring beetles
nodes.desc: Beetle grubs tunnelling in trees. They are the main food of the Magellanic woodpecker.

nodes.name: Magellanic woodpecker
nodes.desc: A big woodpecker of mature southern beech forest that eats mainly wood-boring grubs and beetles, plus spiders.

nodes.name: Patagonian fox
nodes.desc: A small fox of steppe and scrub. Where it shares ground with the culpeo it eats more rodents and is pushed out of prey-rich areas.

nodes.name: Culpeo
nodes.desc: A larger fox that takes hares, rodents, fruit and carrion, and sometimes young guanacos.

nodes.name: Southern caracara
nodes.desc: A bold raptor and scavenger of open country. GloBI records it eating hares, birds and carrion.

nodes.name: Andean condor
nodes.desc: A huge scavenger that glides over the steppe and ice field, feeding on carcasses of guanacos, hares and livestock.

nodes.name: Puma
nodes.desc: The top predator. It hunts guanacos and huemul and is the only natural predator of the huemul.

nodes.name: Southern Patagonian Ice Field
nodes.desc: The great ice cap feeds dozens of glaciers such as Perito Moreno, which end in Lake Argentino and shape the valleys and rivers.

nodes.name: Westerly rain and snow
nodes.desc: The Andes catch Pacific moisture on the west side, leaving the steppe to the east dry. This sets the line between forest and grassland.

nodes.name: Short summer sun
nodes.desc: Long summer days power a brief growing season.

nodes.name: Cold forest and steppe soil
nodes.desc: Young glacial soils that recycle nutrients slowly in the cold.

nodes.name: Fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and soil invertebrates that break down fallen leaves, wood and carcasses.
